record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: Among all immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, is the critical catenoid the only one whose Morse index is equal to 4, up to rigid motions of B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 6. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions) immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 with Morse index 4?
Theorem 5.5 (Tran [100], Smith-Zhou [96], Devyver [19]). The Morse index of the critical catenoid K in B^3 is equal to 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the closed unit ball. A free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ is a (smooth) immersed surface $\Sigma \looparrowright B^3$ whose mean curvature vanishes identically and whose boundary $\partial\Sigma$ lies on $\partial B^3 = S^2$ and meets $S^2$ orthogonally. The Morse index of such a surface is the number of negative eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the second variation (Jacobi) quadratic form for the area functional under variations whose boundary is free to move along $S^2$.

The critical catenoid $K \subset B^3$ is the unique (up to rotation) piece of a Euclidean catenoid that meets $\partial B^3$ orthogonally; it is rotationally symmetric, embedded, and has Morse index equal to $4$.

Question: Is $K$, up to rigid motions of $B^3$, the only immersed free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ whose Morse index is equal to $4$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem appears to remain open. Partial progress is known: any non-flat free boundary minimal surface in $B^3$ has index at least 4, and within the class of free boundary minimal annuli, index 4 characterizes the critical catenoid. A full classification of all immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in $B^3$ with index 4 (without topological restrictions) has not been established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: The Morse index of the critical catenoid
status_evidence.snippet: The rotationally symmetric free boundary minimal catenoid in the unit ball in R^3 has Morse index equal to 4.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that the critical catenoid has index 4.

status_evidence.title: Index Characterization for Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: A free boundary minimal annulus in B^3 has Morse index 4 if and only if it is the critical catenoid.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the index-4 characterization within the class of annuli, leaving the general case open.

status_evidence.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball: recent advances and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Open Question 6. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions) immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 with Morse index 4?
status_evidence.claim: The general question is explicitly listed as open.
